decisions.reason: The firm gave this product its own web page, and it sits close to its core airside operations offer, so results appear to meet aspirations, and a growing, expanding firm has the slack to keep it.
This connectivity module builds on the installed apron equipment and fits the data-integration strategy, and the firm's slack lets it carry the product despite low visibility so far.
Billing software is further from the operational core and only mentioned on the website, so it carries more risk of falling short, but expansion and slack argue against dropping it yet.
Equipment monitoring supports the firm's maintenance and lifecycle service business with its installed base, which makes satisfactory results likely.
Resource management is close to the established offer and complements turnaround management, so there is little shortfall to trigger problemistic search.
A safety alert service for controllers extends the firm's tower and traffic control expertise and serves its safety value proposition, and the slack from growth supports keeping it.
